objective: A project's line is the branch its work ships from (main, staging, any branch it names) and where Nightshift's responsibility ends: programs start from it, the composer starts from the line's own head and merges only queued ranges onto it, each conflict is resolved once on the branch that ships, a protected line holds with its reason instead of looping, and promotion beyond the line is the project's own CI/CD. The authority is the plan document stored with this contract.

successCriteria.outcome: A project whose line is its default branch (main) has every program's ranges composed onto main as they land, with conflicts repaired there, and nothing else merged into the line; the foodfly stall (main does not compose onto the line) cannot occur.

A project may name any branch as its line (main, staging, another); a program of a project with a line starts from that branch, and plan check refuses a contract whose base branch is another one, saying how to fix it.

A line branch that refuses Nightshift's push holds the line with a reason and remediation the owner can read in nightshift line status, and nothing is recomposed until the refusal is cleared; a line run is only created once it is admitted, so a full org ceiling leaves no interrupted runs behind. A line run that parked work says so by ending failed, and parked work can be sent back to the queue.

The architecture record, the skills and a run's report describe the line as the branch work ships from: programs start from it, work reaches it whole or in part, unfinished user-facing work stays unreachable until its program completes, and promotion beyond it is the project's.

constraints: A project with no line behaves exactly as it does today.
Program runs, strands and their landing are unchanged; the line's queue, path reservation, repair budget and parking (P24) are kept.
The publisher only ever moves a line branch by compare-and-swap; nothing forces a push, and nothing edits a repository's branch protection.
Nothing in this program changes a project repository, its pipeline or its configuration; that is the owner's.
Windows keeps working: nothing added assumes a POSIX shell or path.

forbiddenActions: edit another program's documents under docs/programs/
change any repository other than this one

stories.who: The owner running several programs in parallel on one project
stories.problem: The line resolves a conflict between two programs on a preview branch, then the second program's pull request meets the same conflict at main and someone resolves it again, differently; main and the line diverge, main stops merging onto the line, and every later range parks.
stories.outcome: Programs compose straight onto the branch that ships, whole or in part, as they land; each conflict is resolved once, there; the line keeps moving.
words: in one instance it required another agent to merge the program branches into main and resolve conflicts. Whereas, I thought the conflicts would be resolved by nightshift
I'd rather the line continually move forward (whole or part program) and merge into main (even if it contains a half-program)

stories.who: A team using Nightshift with its own way of shipping
stories.problem: The line can only be a preview beside main, so a team that ships from main, or promotes a staging branch to production, cannot point Nightshift at the branch its pipeline uses.
stories.outcome: The team names its line branch in nightshift.config.json, Nightshift composes onto that branch and stops there, and the team's own CI/CD decides what happens next.
words: i also want to give some latitude for other devs/users to organize their CI/CD the way they want. I feel like we should just allow a config for the "line branch"

acceptance: The composer starts each batch from the line's own head and merges only queued ranges; the default-branch fetch, the main merge and the 'main does not compose onto the line' park are gone; a line branch absent at the remote is created from the default branch's head

A protected or forbidden line push records a waiting reason with the remediation on the line and is not recomposed until a new landing or the line's retry tries it once more
A line run is created only after admission; a refusal records the line's waiting reason and leaves no run

nightshift line requeue [<program> | --all] moves parked entries back to the queue with their repair count reset, records who asked and starts a line run; engine principals are refused
The line end-to-end test proves a line on the default branch, a direct push to the line between batches, and a protected line branch

decisions.question: Does Nightshift keep a preview line mode (a line nothing promotes from, with programs reaching main through their own pull requests)?
options: Retire it: a line is always the branch work ships from (main, or a staging branch the project promotes)
Keep it as an option beside shipping lines
decisions.leaning: Retire it: a line is always the branch work ships from (main, or a staging branch the project promotes)
decisions.answer: Retire it: a line is always the branch work ships from (main, or a staging branch the project promotes)
decisions.rationale: The preview mode resolves every cross-program conflict twice and the two resolutions diverge (foodfly, 2026-10-31); a team wanting review before main uses a staging line.

decisions.question: When a project has a line, do its programs start from the line branch?
options: Yes, always: the contract inherits its base branch from the line and plan check refuses another
No: the contract's base branch stays independent
decisions.leaning: Yes, always: the contract inherits its base branch from the line and plan check refuses another
decisions.answer: Yes, always: the contract inherits its base branch from the line and plan check refuses another
decisions.rationale: Each program builds on everything already on the line, so conflicts with it surface while the program is built, not at composition.

decisions.question: Does the composer still merge the repository's default branch into the line before composing?
options: No: the line's inputs are its own head and the queued ranges
Yes, with a budgeted repair job when it does not merge
decisions.leaning: No: the line's inputs are its own head and the queued ranges
decisions.answer: No: the line's inputs are its own head and the queued ranges
decisions.rationale: Nightshift's responsibility ends at the line; with the line on main nothing else exists, and a staging line's hotfix flow is the project's CI's. It removes the stall class seen on foodfly.

outOfScope: Promotion, release tags, deploys and a release or candidate view (a later program can build on the line's composition records)
Feature-flag tooling: unfinished work is kept unreachable by convention
Any change to a project's own repository, pipeline or configuration
